sanskrit: aham manur abhavaṁ sūryaś cāhaṁ kakṣīvām̐ ṛṣir asmi vipraḥ | ahaṁ kutsam ārjuneyaṁ ny ṛñje 'haṁ kavir uśanā paśyatā mā ||
english: I became Manu, and I am Sūrya; I am the inspired seer Kakṣīvān. I have subdued Kutsa, the son of Arjuna; I am the poet Uśanā — behold me!

sanskrit: aham bhūmim adadām āryāyāhaṁ vṛṣṭiṁ dāśuṣe martyāya | aham apo anayaṁ vāvaśānā mama devāso anu ketam āyan ||
english: I gave the earth to the Ārya; I gave rain to the mortal who offers sacrifice. I led the roaring waters; the gods followed after my will.

sanskrit: aham puro mandasāno vy airaṁ nava sākaṁ navatīḥ śambarasya | śatatamaṁ veśyaṁ sarvatātā divodāsam atithigvaṁ yad āvam ||
english: Exhilarated, I burst open Śambara's ninety-nine fortresses all at once; and the hundredth, his stronghold, when I aided Divodāsa Atithigva with my whole might.

sanskrit: pra su ṣa vibhyo maruto vir astu pra śyenaḥ śyenebhya āśupatvā | acakrayā yat svadhayā suparṇo havyam bharan manave devajuṣṭam ||
english: Let the bird be pre-eminent among the Maruts; let the falcon outfly the other falcons in swift flight — that fair-winged one who, effortlessly and by his own power, carried the oblation dear to the gods to Manu.

sanskrit: bharad yadi vir ato vevijānaḥ pathoruṇā manojavā asarji | tūyaṁ yayau madhunā somyenota śravo vivide śyeno atra ||
english: As the quivering bird bore it from there and was released along the broad path swift as thought, quickly the falcon sped with the sweet soma-draught, and here the bird found glory.

sanskrit: ṛjīpī śyeno dadamāno aṁśum parāvataḥ śakuno mandram madam | somam bharad dādṛhāṇo devāvān divo amuṣmād uttarād ādāya ||
english: The straight-flying falcon, the bird bestowing the soma-stalk, bringing sweet exhilaration from afar, carried the soma, firm-gripped, protected by the gods, taking it from yonder upper heaven.

sanskrit: ādāya śyeno abharat somaṁ sahasraṁ savām̐ ayutaṁ ca sākam | atrā puraṁdhir ajahād arātīr made somasya mūrā amūraḥ ||
english: Having seized it, the falcon brought the soma — a thousand pressings and ten thousand together. Here the wise one, in the intoxication of soma, abandoned the foes; the fool-free one left foolish enemies behind.

sanskrit: garbhe nu sann anv eṣām avedam ahaṁ devānāṁ janimāni viśvā | śatam mā pura āyasīr arakṣann adha śyeno javasā nir adīyam ||
english: While still in the womb I came to know all the births of these gods. A hundred iron fortresses guarded me; yet then, as the falcon, I flew forth with speed.

sanskrit: na ghā sa mām apa joṣaṁ jabhārābhīm āsa tvakṣasā vīryeṇa | īrmā puraṁdhir ajahād arātīr uta vātām̐ atarac chūśuvānaḥ ||
english: He indeed did not detain me willingly; he charged against me with vigorous might. But the wise one forsook the foes, and, surging forth, he passed beyond the winds.

sanskrit: ava yac chyeno asvanīd adha dyor vi yad yadi vāta ūhuḥ puraṁdhim | sṛjad yad asmā ava ha kṣipaj jyāṁ kṛśānur astā manasā bhuraṇyan ||
english: When the falcon screamed downward from heaven, when the winds perhaps carried the wise one away — when Kṛśānu the archer, vibrating in his mind, let fly the bowstring aiming at the bird —

sanskrit: ṛjipya īm indrāvato na bhujyuṁ śyeno jabhāra bṛhato adhi ṣṇoḥ | antaḥ patat patatry asya parṇam adha yāmani prasitasya tad veḥ ||
english: The straight-flying falcon carried it, as Indra carried Bhujyu from the vast height; as the feathered one flew, a feather fell from the bird in its swift course.

sanskrit: adha śvetaṁ kalaśaṁ gobhir aktam āpipyānam maghavā śukram andhaḥ | adhvaryubhiḥ prayatam madhvo agram indro madāya prati dhat pibadhyai śūro madāya prati dhat pibadhyai ||
english: Then the white bowl, anointed with the milk of kine, brimming with the bright, sweet drink — the first portion of the soma set forth by the adhvaryus — Indra the mighty received for his exhilaration, to drink; the hero received it for his joy, to drink.

sanskrit: tvā yujā tava tat soma sakhya indro apo manave sasrutas kaḥ | ahann ahim ariṇāt sapta sindhūn apāvṛṇod apihiteva khāni ||
english: With you as ally — that was your deed, O Soma, your friendship — Indra caused the waters to flow for Manu. He slew the serpent, he released the seven rivers, he uncovered the channels as it were blocked up.

sanskrit: tvā yujā ni khidat sūryasyendraś cakraṁ sahasā sadya indo | adhi ṣṇunā bṛhatā vartamānam maho druho apa viśvāyu dhāyi ||
english: With you as ally, Indra at once forcibly pressed down the wheel of Sūrya, O Indu. As it rolled on the great height, he swept away the great deceiver; he was freed from all treachery.

sanskrit: ahann indro adahad agnir indo purā dasyūn madhyaṁdinād abhīke | durge duroṇe kratvā na yātām purū sahasrā śarvā ni barhīt ||
english: Indra slew, Agni burned, O Indu; the Dasyus confronted them at midday in hostile encounter. With no way to pass through the difficult pass and the stronghold, he crushed full many thousands with his shafts.

sanskrit: viśvasmāt sīm adhamām̐ indra dasyūn viśo dāsīr akṛṇor apraśastāḥ | abādhethām amṛṇataṁ ni śatrūn avindethām apacitiṁ vadhatraiḥ ||
english: You two thrust down the Dasyus from every side, O Indra; you made the Dāsa peoples reviled. You two oppressed and crushed the enemies; you two found retribution with your weapons.

sanskrit: evā satyam maghavānā yuvaṁ tad indraś ca somorvam aśvyaṁ goḥ | ādardṛtam apihitāny aśnā riricathuḥ kṣāś cit tatṛdānā ||
english: Even so truly, O bountiful ones — you two, Indra and Soma — you won the wide space rich in horses and cattle. Bursting open the closed-up places with a stone, you two, rending even the rocks, left them empty.

sanskrit: ā naḥ stuta upa vājebhir ūtī indra yāhi haribhir mandasānaḥ | tiraś cid aryaḥ savanā purūṇy āṅgūṣebhir gṛṇānaḥ satyarādhāḥ ||
english: Come to us when praised, Indra, with your aids and prizes; come, exhilarated, with your bay steeds. Though past the stranger's pressings, hearing our lauds, you whose bounty is true.

sanskrit: ā hi ṣmā yāti naryaś cikitvān hūyamānaḥ sotṛbhir upa yajñam | svaśvo yo abhīrur manyamānaḥ suṣvāṇebhir madati saṁ ha vīraiḥ ||
english: For he, the manly one, ever discerning, comes when called by the pressers to the sacrifice; he who, with fine horses and fearless spirit, exults with the well-pressing men and with heroes.

sanskrit: śrāvayed asya karṇā vājayadhyai juṣṭām anu pra diśam mandayadhyai | udvāvṛṣāṇo rādhase tuviṣmān karan na indraḥ sutīrthābhayaṁ ca ||
english: Let his ears be made to hear, so that he wins the prize; let him be gladdened along the favored direction. Rearing up mightily for the gift, may Indra make for us a safe ford and freedom from fear.

sanskrit: acchā yo gantā nādhamānam ūtī itthā vipraṁ hava mānaṁ gṛṇantam | upa tmani dadhāno dhury ā3śūn sahasrāṇi śatāni vajrabāhuḥ ||
english: He who will come with help to the supplicant — thus truly, to the inspired poet calling and lauding him — placing upon himself swiftly his swift steeds, he of the thunderbolt-arm, thousands upon hundreds.

sanskrit: tvotāso maghavann indra viprā vayaṁ te syāma sūrayo gṛṇantaḥ | bhejānāso bṛhaddivasya rāya ākāyyasya dāvane purukṣoḥ ||
english: Strengthened by you, O bountiful Indra, we inspired poets would be your worshippers giving praise, partaking of the vast celestial wealth, to be given from the plentiful, inexhaustible treasure.

sanskrit: nakir indra tvad uttaro na jyāyām̐ asti vṛtrahan | nakir evā yathā tvam ||
english: None is higher than you, O Indra, none greater exists, O Vṛtra-slayer; none is truly as you are.

sanskrit: satrā te anu kṛṣṭayo viśvā cakreva vāvṛtuḥ | satrā mahām̐ asi śrutaḥ ||
english: All peoples have turned toward you together, as spokes around a wheel. Truly great and renowned you are.

sanskrit: viśve caned anā tvā devāsa indra yuyudhuḥ | yad ahā naktam ātiraḥ ||
english: Not even all the gods together could fight you without blemish, O Indra, when you traversed the day and the night.

sanskrit: yatrota bādhitebhyaś cakraṁ kutsāya yudhyate | muṣāya indra sūryam ||
english: Where, fighting for Kutsa among the beleaguered, you stole the sun's wheel, O Indra.

sanskrit: yatra devām̐ ṛghāyato viśvām̐ ayudhya eka it | tvam indra vanūm̐r ahan ||
english: Where you alone fought all the raging gods — you, Indra, slew the challengers.

sanskrit: yatrota martyāya kam ariṇā indra sūryam | prāvaḥ śacībhir etaśam ||
english: Where, O Indra, you released the sun for a certain mortal, and with your powers you aided Etaśa.

sanskrit: kim ād utāsi vṛtrahan maghavan manyumattamaḥ | atrāha dānum ātiraḥ ||
english: What then were you, O Vṛtra-slayer, most passionate in fury, O bountiful one? Here you crossed over Dānu.

sanskrit: etad ghed uta vīryam indra cakartha pauṁsyam | striyaṁ yad durhaṇāyuvaṁ vadhīr duhitaraṁ divaḥ ||
english: This too was a deed of virile heroism you performed, O Indra: that you struck down the wickedly-plotting woman, the daughter of Heaven.

sanskrit: divaś cid ghā duhitaram mahān mahīyamānām | uṣāsam indra sam piṇak ||
english: Even the great daughter of Heaven — Uṣas, swelling with pride — O Indra, you shattered her.

sanskrit: apoṣā anasaḥ sarat sampiṣṭād aha bibhyuṣī | ni yat sīṁ śiśnathad vṛṣā ||
english: Then Uṣas fled from her crushed chariot in fear, when the bull-god struck her down.

sanskrit: etad asyā anaḥ śaye susampiṣṭaṁ vipāśy ā | sasāra sīm parāvataḥ ||
english: Her chariot lies there, utterly crushed beside the Vipāś river; she has fled to the far distance.

sanskrit: uta sindhuṁ vibālyaṁ vitasthānām adhi kṣami | pari ṣṭhā indra māyayā ||
english: And the Sindhu river, swelling wide, spread across the land of those who stood apart; O Indra, you controlled it with your power.

sanskrit: uta śuṣṇasya dhṛṣṇuyā pra mṛkṣo abhi vedanam | puro yad asya sampiṇak ||
english: And with boldness against Śuṣṇa you wiped out his abode, when you crushed his fortresses.

sanskrit: uta dāsaṁ kaulitaram bṛhataḥ parvatād adhi | avāhann indra śambaram ||
english: And Śambara the Dāsa, son of Kulitara, you hurled down, O Indra, from the great mountain.

sanskrit: uta dāsasya varcinaḥ sahasrāṇi śatāvadhīḥ | adhi pañca pradhīm̐r iva ||
english: And of the Dāsa Varcin you slew thousands — a hundred — over the five peoples, as it were.

sanskrit: uta tyam putram agruvaḥ parāvṛktaṁ śatakratuḥ | uktheṣv indra ābhajat ||
english: And that son of Agru, rejected and cast aside — Indra of a hundred powers made him a sharer in the lauds.

sanskrit: uta tyā turvaśāyadū asnātārā śacīpatiḥ | indro vidvām̐ apārayat ||
english: And those two — Turvaśa and Yadu — who had not bathed, the lord of powers, Indra, knowing the way, carried them across.

sanskrit: uta tyā sadya āryā sarayor indra pārataḥ | arṇācitrarathāvadhīḥ ||
english: And those Āryans — on the far bank of the Sarayu — Arṇa and Citraratha you slew at once, O Indra.

sanskrit: anu dvā jahitā nayo 'ndhaṁ śroṇaṁ ca vṛtrahan | na tat te sumnam aṣṭave ||
english: Two abandoned ones you led — the blind and the lame — O Vṛtra-slayer; that grace of yours is not to be attained by effort.

sanskrit: śatam aśmanmayīnām purām indro vy āsyat | divodāsāya dāśuṣe ||
english: A hundred stone-built fortresses Indra burst open for Divodāsa who offered sacrifice.

sanskrit: asvāpayad dabhītaye sahasrā triṁśataṁ hathaiḥ | dāsānām indro māyayā ||
english: For Dabhīti, Indra put to sleep thirty thousand of the Dāsas with his might and his power of māyā.

sanskrit: sa ghed utāsi vṛtrahan samāna indra gopatiḥ | yas tā viśvāni cicyuṣe ||
english: For you are indeed both, O Vṛtra-slayer — at once, O Indra, the lord-protector who has gathered all these things.

sanskrit: uta nūnaṁ yad indriyaṁ kariṣyā indra pauṁsyam | adyā nakiṣ ṭad ā minat ||
english: And whatever heroic deed of Indra-might you shall yet perform, O Indra — not even today can any diminish that.

sanskrit: vāmaṁ-vāmaṁ ta ādure devo dadātv aryamā | vāmam pūṣā vāmam bhago vāmaṁ devaḥ karūḻatī ||
english: May divine Aryamā grant you desirable things, one beautiful gift after another; may Pūṣan grant beauty, may Bhaga grant beauty, may the god Karūḻatī grant beauty.
